newsitem.title: USA: NYC Council extends tax surcharge, looks to Albany.
newsitem.headline: NYC Council extends tax surcharge, looks to Albany.

text.p: The New York City Council voted Monday to support renewing a 12.5 percent surcharge on the city personal income tax.

The 45-to-3 vote was necessary before the state legislature could renew the tax, which expired at year-end when Albany failed to act on it during a special legislative session. This created big risks in the city's budget, the state and city comptrollers have said.
The tax was created to support former Mayor David Dinkins "Safe Streets, Safe City Program," helping to pay for an additional 7,000 police officers.

During a hearing before the council, city officials said that the tax would produce $406 million during fiscal 1998. The city stands to lose up $463 million if the tax is not renewed by Albany lawmakers, in part because of its effect on other revenues.

Council officials said they advanced their vote because they expected quick approval from Albany, saying a memorandum of understanding had been agreed between Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, City Council Speaker, Peter Vallone, and the Senate and Assembly leaders.

A spokeswoman for the Senate Majority Leader, Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, said that body might act as soon as this week. A spokeswoman for Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, was not immediately available to comment.

Under the agreement, the city pledged to keep the present number of police officers. It would pay penalites, in the form of a reduction in how much of the surcharge it could collect, if the size of the force fell more than two percent below the present total of 38,100 police officers, city officials said.
The pact also requires New York City to honor the capital commitments for the Board of Education set forth in the city's present budget for both fiscal 1997 and 1998.

The income tax surcharge, which the city has continued to collect even though it expired, was extended through the end of 1998, and made retroactive until January 1, according to the Council's version.
